notes.title: Devlog: Where Did the Idea Come From?
notes.notes: [p]Remember during the pandemic everyone started a "lockdown project"?  —  Mine was a video game to practice drawing. Well it's now 2025,  and my “lockdown project” is finally starting to take shape, so I thought it's about time I made the first devlog for —  [i]Figure Drawing Garden.[/i][/p][p][/p][h3][b]ORIGIN OF THE IDEA...[/b][/h3][p]Back in 2020, before the world came to a complete stop, I was on Erasmus in Paris, studying animation at Gobelins L'École de L’Image. My favorite thing to do while there was draw in the Louvre's magnificent sculpture gardens. Every time I visited, without fail, there would be at least a dozen artists drawing these incredible sculptures. I remember feeling extremely fortunate to be able to draw there, and at the same time —[b] envious that such an valuable resource wasn’t something I had access to at home.[/b][/p][p]Then the pandemic hit. I moved back to Ireland, and the contrast couldn’t have been sharper — I went from exploring a city overflowing with ateliers and galleries, to being confined to my bedroom with no statues to draw at all.[/p][p]Then one day, when I really had an itch to do some figure drawing, I came up with a simple solution — a flat plane in Unity with a couple of sculptures dropped onto it, just so I’d have something to practice with. [b]It was basic, made only for my own use… but it was a step towards how it felt to draw in that sculpture garden at the Louvre[/b] — and the start of what would eventually become [i]Figure Drawing Garden[/i].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45341326/9590b9dc34674374c0911895890e3774977ae669.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]GETTING CARRIED AWAY...[/b][/h3][p align="start"]But after doing a drawing or two, I quickly found myself… distracted. Instead of sketching, I kept tinkering. First I adjusted the lighting, then added fog, then some ambient audio. Every time I sat down to draw, I’d think of a new way to improve the tool.[/p][p align="start"]I realized I could set up custom lighting however I liked, I could overlay three-dimensional perspective grids to guide proportions. I could even simplify a figure down to its most basic shapes. [b]Before long, my simple flat plane had grown into an immersive, procedurally generated garden[/b] and the basic models I had started with were replaced with beautiful scans of real sculptures— including some from the very same garden at the Louvre.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45341326/a6de34f242947da1b60cbc2571dfcdb3d43b37d3.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]FIVE YEARS LATER...[/b][/h3][p align="start"][i]Figure Drawing Garden[/i] has come a long way from that flat plane of models back in 2020. Today, it features an exquisite collection of classical and Renaissance [b]sculpture scans[/b] so that you can study directly from the masters. Your garden [b]expands as you draw,[/b] and drawing tools like [b]Dynamic Lighting[/b] help you practice shading, while the [b]Perspective Grid[/b] and [b]Simplified Form[/b] modes are [b]beginner friendly[/b]. For an extra twist, rare [b]Challenge Sculptures[/b] introduce new techniques and keep things exciting.[/p][p align="start"]And next, I'll be adding support for [b]community-made Modelpacks — [/b]allowing players to customize their gardens and draw any models they choose![/p][p][/p][h3][b]FEEL LIKE DRAWING?[/b][/h3][list][*][p][url="https://joshocaoimh.itch.io/figure-drawing-garden"]Download the free demo[/url] and grab your sketchbook, relax, explore, and draw. [/p][/*][*][p] Art is more fun together, so hop into the [url="https://discord.gg/vu8pTfMsBZ"]Discord[/url]— share your drawings, get inspired, and grow alongside fellow artists.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45341326/785e9c4137d2ebf2ccba9fb69c1e8fed59b660f4.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p]
